## OVERVIEW

In Unit 4 we learn about social network analysis as a both a theory and a method and look at specific examples of its use in educational contexts. The required and self-selected readings for this week provide an introduction to SNA in the field of education, including the historical, theoretical, and analytical foundations of a social network perspective. Our primary goal this week is to build a basic understanding of SNA as an approach to understand and improve student learning and the contexts in which learning occurs.

## READINGS

For Unit 4, you will read Chapter 1 from [Social Network Analysis and Education](https://methods-sagepub-com.prox.lib.ncsu.edu/book/mono/social-network-analysis-and-education/toc) (Carolan 2014) and locate one additional research article, presentation, or informal study to help address our discussion questions for the week.

### SNA and Education Part I: Theory and Concepts

The following chapter illustrates how social network analysis provides educational researchers with a different way of thinking about and measuring an learning processes and outcomes by that explicitly account for the importance of one's relationships with others, as well as the larger pattern in which these relationships are embedded.

-   [Chapter 1: The Social Network Perspective and Educational Research Introduction](https://methods-sagepub-com.prox.lib.ncsu.edu/book/social-network-analysis-and-education/n1.xml)

    Carolan, B. V. (2014). *Chapter 1: The Social Network Perspective and Educational Research.* In *Social Network Analysis and Education: Theory, Methods & Applications*. Sage.

### Self-Selected Resource

Use the [NCSU Library](https://www.lib.ncsu.edu/#articles), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/) or search engine of your choice to locate a journal article, presentation, website or other scholarly resource that uses the social network perspective to analyze a topic of interest. Your selection should also address one or more of the discussion topics/questions provided below. In addition, you are welcome to find less formal resources such as videos or shorter online articles to share with the class and that help us better understand this week's topics for discussion.

## DISCUSSION

Our “in-class” conversation happens in the forum. Build on peers’ ideas and ground points in the readings.

### What to post (your 3 posts + 1 reply)

### 1) Carolan Ch. 1: The Social Network Perspective and Educational Research Introduction

Choose **one**:

-   Consider a real or hypothetical network you’re part of (e.g., a course cohort, school team, online community).

    Who are the **actors**? What **ties** connect them? Are there identifiable **groups/communities**? What makes this collection a **social network**?

-   Which aspect of the social network perspective (interdependence of actors, ties as resource channels, or social structure as opportunity/constraint) best illuminates a learning problem you care about—and **why**?

-   Draft a research question that **requires relational data**. What relations would you measure, and at what **level** (ego, dyad, triad, or complete network)? Why that level?

### 2) Applied SNA Design (mini study plan)

Post a short plan for applying SNA to an educational context of your choice:

-   **Context & question**: What learning problem or process are you investigating?
-   **Actors & ties**: Who are the nodes? What tie(s) will you measure (e.g., co-work, feedback, help-seeking, replies)?
-   **Data & level**: How will you collect relational data (survey, logs, observations)? At what level (ego, dyad, triad, complete), and why?
-   **Measures/analysis**: Which basic metrics or models might you use (e.g., degree/betweenness centrality, density, community detection, ERGM, SIENA)?
-   **Use & equity**: How might insights inform actionable “change ideas” (e.g., fostering bridging ties, redesigning groupings), and what ethical safeguards will you put in place?

### 3) Self-Selected Resource

Provide a brief overview of your self-selected resource that includes the following:

-   APA Citation (note: this can be easily [retrieved via Google Scholar](https://libanswers.ucmerced.edu/faq/95935))
-   **Purpose** of the study/resource
-   **Network level** measured (ego, dyad, triad, complete) and **why**
-   **Relations** measured among actors (e.g., collaboration, advice-seeking, replies) and why those (and not others)
-   How the work emphasizes one or more of these SNA premises:
    -   Interdependence of actors
    -   Ties as channels for resources/information
    -   Social structure as opportunity/constraint
    -   Structure as an **enduring** pattern of relations
-   **Key findings/implications** and intended **beneficiaries** (e.g., teachers, students, leaders)
-   **Limitations/ethics** (consent, privacy, re-identification risks, power dynamics)

At minimum, your collective posts should also help us interpret or elaborate on discussion topics, questions, or ideas others have shared by "making connection to the learning materials" and should reference at some point the required video, course text and your self-selected resource.

### Productive Online Discussion Model

#### **Disposition 1: Discuss to Comprehend**

Actively engage in such cognitive processes as interpretation, elaboration, **making connections to** prior knowledge.

-   Interpreting or elaborating the ideas by making connection to the **learning materials**
-   Interpreting or elaborating the ideas by making connection to **personal experience**
-   Interpreting or elaborating the ideas by making connection to other **ideas, sources, or references**

#### **Disposition 2: Discuss to Critique**

Carefully **examine other people's views**, and be sensitive and analytical to conflicting views.

-   Building or **adding new insights or ideas** to others' posts
-   **Challenging ideas** in the texts
-   Challenging ideas in others' posts

#### **Disposition 3: Discuss to Construct Knowledge**

Actively **negotiate meanings**, and be ready to reconsider, refine and sometimes revise their thinking.

-   **Comparing views** from the texts or others' posts
-   Facilitating thinking and discussions by **raising questions**
-   Refining and **revising one's own view** based on the texts or others' posts

#### **Disposition 4: Discuss to Share Improved Understanding**

Actively **synthesize knowledge** and explicitly express improved understanding based on a review of previous discussions.

-   **Summarizing personal learning** experiences of online discussions

-   **Synthesizing content** of discussion

-   **Generating new topics** based on a review of previous discussions
